newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks end down on retail profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks end down on retail profit-taking.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed down for a third day in a row as profit-taking by small retail investors continued to take its toll on the market, brokers said.
The Colombo Stock Exchange all share index ended 2.9 points down to close at 622.7.
Turnover was 62.4 million rupees, supported by 245,000 John Keells Holdings -- up three rupees to 195 -- and an overnight packet of 1.2 million Seylan Merchant Bank at 6.75.
"We didn't find much participation by foreigners and local institutions today. The activity was mostly retail," said Ralph Wijesinghe, manager foreign sales at Asia Stock Brokers.
Losses outnumbered gains 25 to 14. Plantation company Bogawantalawa shed eight rupees to 42 rupees, while food firm Ceylon Cold Stores was down 6.75 to 69.25.

Some brokers said they expected the rest of the week to be dull as the Sri Lankan capital was placed on full alert for possible attacks by separatist Tamil Tigers during their "Heroes' Week", when rebels attack to honour fallen fighters.
"The entire business community is keeping a low profile this week. Everyone's adopted a wait-and-see attitude," a broker for Bartleet Mallory said.
